target.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting
target.body:
Related: #1000
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108435

## What This PR Does

This brings the Windows Companion setup path forward to the current OpenClaw beta track and fixes the Companion-side defects found while validating that integration:

- pin the Companion-owned installer to official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2`;
- make compact number labels deterministic under `pt-PT` and other decimal-comma locales;
- coordinate Gateway reload suspension/restoration around the native wizard;
- survive the expected Gateway restart and reconnect during onboarding;
- order keepalive, pairing, revocation recovery, and final setup progress correctly;
- stabilize the affected connection, E2E, and accessibility tests.

This is intentionally a beta-target PR. Maintainer approval of a prerelease default is still required; it is not presented as the stable-channel policy.

## Ownership

- The Windows Companion owns WSL creation, systemd/service lifecycle, Windows Node bootstrap, setup progress, and MXC integration.
- OpenClaw owns the native onboarding wizard and Gateway command runtime.
- The Companion uses the released `wizard.start` contract with an empty parameter object; it does not invent protocol fields.
- No OpenClaw core patch or custom package is included in this PR.

## Current-Head Validation

Final local head: `9c308f0bd13948ccfd3c39d0e7373914fa8d6801`, integrated with upstream main `4518dd87ed2bbfbdb3e1389cd88e2bc95141ea2b`.

- Full repository build: passed, zero warnings/errors.
- Connection: `443/443` passed.
- SetupEngine: `448/448` passed.
- Tray: `1742/1742` passed.
- Shared: `2866` passed; `31` explicit integration skips.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Disposable Companion-owned WSL revocation/reconnect E2E: `1/1` passed.
- Strict Gateway -> Windows Node -> MXC E2E: `2/2` passed, without skip allowance.
- Both E2E runs completed uninstall and removed their temporary WSL distros.

The supported-path proof first installed official beta.2 through the normal Companion flow. Official beta.2 then reproduced the Gateway-loss failure during the native wizard. A separately built OpenClaw package containing the narrow non-exiting wizard-runtime fix was injected only into the disposable proof distro; with that correction, revocation/reconnect and MXC both passed. That package is evidence for a separate OpenClaw PR, not hidden Companion behavior.

## Failed-First Evidence

- Earlier public CI installed official beta.2 but lost the Gateway during the wizard/reconnect path.
- The exact OpenClaw failure was isolated to wizard commands invoking the normal exiting CLI runtime inside the Gateway process.
- The separate OpenClaw fix uses a non-exiting runtime, treats only exit code zero as normal completion, and propagates nonzero exits; its focused tests pass `8/8`, and its official build/pack path passes.
- Current-head Companion E2E succeeds only after that explicit corrected-package injection. Therefore official beta.2 alone remains a known dependency blocker.

## Auto-review

The final public branch diff was reviewed with Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` at high reasoning. One P2 claimed the restart helper uninstalls the service before retrying. Direct call-path inspection rejected it: `StartOrRestartAndWaitForHealthAsync` has no uninstall call; `gateway uninstall` exists only in `InstallGatewayServiceStep.RollbackAsync`, which the restart helper does not invoke. Accepted actionable findings: zero.

## Scope And Security

- No `/new` or session behavior changes.
- No token, secret, model, memory, plugin, or agent-policy changes.
- No new permissions or network destinations.
- No broader command authority.
- No operator runtime was installed or mutated for validation.

## Review State

- [x] Current `main` integrated without force-pushing.
- [x] Source, focused suites, full build, and strict MXC proof passed on the final local head.
- [x] Failed-first official beta.2 behavior is documented rather than masked.
- [ ] Fresh GitHub CI on the updated head.
- [ ] Separate OpenClaw wizard-runtime fix reviewed/landed, or beta package updated with an equivalent fix.
- [ ] Maintainer approval of the beta-default release contract.

This PR is ready for review as the Windows Companion side of the beta integration. It should not merge as a claim that unmodified official beta.2 already passes the complete setup path.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized operator/agent engineering record</summary>

- This PR was developed across a multi-day operator/agent recovery and validation effort, not as a mechanical version bump.
- The operator required the Windows Companion to remain the owner of WSL creation, service lifecycle, Windows Node, and MXC, while OpenClaw remains the owner of the native onboarding wizard.
- Early attempts exposed a stale release target, culture-sensitive compact-number formatting, wizard reconnect failures, pairing/revocation ordering problems, and test-harness flakes. Each accepted in-scope issue was corrected and rerun instead of being hidden with sleeps, disabled tests, or a custom production installer.
- The release target moved to official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2` after that beta became available. The branch was then integrated with the latest Windows Node `main`, preserving newer upstream pairing and telemetry fixes rather than duplicating them.
- Official beta.2 installed through the real Companion-owned WSL path but lost the Gateway during the native wizard. Investigation isolated the defect to OpenClaw's Gateway wizard runtime, not the Companion installer.
- A separate, narrow OpenClaw correction was built and packaged. The Companion test harness first installed official beta.2 normally, then injected the corrected package only in the disposable proof distro. That correction is not hidden in this PR.
- Final-head automated proof passed: Connection `443/443`, SetupEngine `448/448`, Tray `1742/1742`, Shared `2866` plus `31` explicit integration skips.
- Final-head supported-path proof passed: revocation/reconnect `1/1`; strict Gateway-to-Windows-Node-to-MXC `2/2`, including a protected-write denial; both runs uninstalled and removed their temporary WSL distros.
- Final Auto-review reported one restart/uninstall concern. Direct call-path inspection showed the claimed uninstall branch does not exist in the restart helper, so no speculative code was added.
- No operator secrets, tokens, private messages, raw prompts, or runtime data are included in this transcript.

</details>

target.title: fix: show readable session names across Windows UX
target.body:
Closes #981

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users opening session pickers, the Sessions page, or tray menus would see opaque Gateway routing keys and machine-like IDs, especially for channel, heartbeat, subagent, cron, and TUI sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consumes the Gateway’s additive session `presentation` contract, preserves the raw key only for routing, and keeps a conservative fallback for older Gateways. Friendly titles now use explicit labels and Gateway presentation metadata; background sessions are hidden by default with an opt-in toggle, while an explicitly active background chat remains selectable.

The fallback recognizes only established built-in key families and treats the remaining key tail as opaque text, shortening UUID/hash runs instead of teaching WinUI every Gateway routing grammar.

## User Impact

Session surfaces show useful names instead of values such as `agent:main:tui-847241c7-…:heartbeat`. Foreground chats are easier to find, duplicate friendly names remain distinguishable, account/agent/node context appears as secondary text, and routing continues to use the exact original session key.

## Evidence

- Shared resolver and parser tests cover Gateway presentation precedence, configured main-session keys, all built-in fallback families, opaque-ID redaction, and default/opt-in background visibility.
- Tray tests cover duplicate-title stability, Gateway agent grouping, background picker behavior, dashboard/tray foreground selection, and unchanged routing IDs.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Native Windows CI passed on commit `80dbd80a`: 2,815 Shared, 1,716 Tray, 422 Connection, 126 WinNode CLI, 18 Tray integration, 10 functional UI, 423 SetupEngine, 78 Tray UI, and 19 accessibility tests.
- All three native E2E shards passed: 16 setup/connect, 1 revocation/recovery, and 2 network/recovery tests executed successfully.
- Release builds and uploaded artifacts passed for both `win-x64` and `win-arm64`.
- Build and Test run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/29291054905

## Real Behavior Proof

Collected on July 15, 2026 with the merged Parallels Windows workflows from openclaw/openclaw#107881 and openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#992.

- Environment: Parallels Desktop 26.4, Windows 11 ARM64, .NET 10.0.302, Windows SDK 10.0.26100, and WebView2 150.0.4078.65.
- Actual app path: the repository UI proof launches the real `OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI.exe` in an isolated tray-data directory, navigates the production Hub deep-link path, inspects the rendered WinUI Automation tree, and captures the Hub window.

- Result: both refs built with 0 warnings and 0 errors; the focused real-process UI test passed on both refs.
- Before observation: the second duplicate title exposed the routing-derived qualifier `OpenClaw Windows Tray (main/fork)`.
- After observation: the same row uses the neutral title `OpenClaw Windows Tray (2)`, shows `agent main` as secondary context, and the Sessions page exposes the new `Show background` control.
- Routing proof: UI Automation opened both visible rows and confirmed selection still used the original keys `agent:main:main` and `agent:main:fork`.
- Scope boundary: this deterministic visual pass proves the real Windows rendering, routing, and older-Gateway fallback path. It does not claim a live integrated `sessions.list.presentation` response from openclaw/openclaw#106832.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can see that a Windows node tool failed, but existing telemetry does not explain whether it was rejected by exec policy, blocked before sandbox execution, failed inside the command, timed out, or could not deliver its response. Gateway and local MCP invocations also lack a shared end-to-end diagnostic view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds provider-neutral, privacy-reviewed instrumentation for gateway and MCP node tool calls without changing either protocol. Typed diagnostics preserve command execution semantics while reporting stable outcomes, failure categories, authorization/run phases, sandbox application and fallback details, and response-delivery failures.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose why an agent tool failed from traces, metrics, and bounded failure-only logs. `system.run` telemetry distinguishes exec-policy denial, unsupported sandbox requests, MXC availability/fallback, command failure, timeout, and transport failure without exporting command arguments, payloads, output, paths, credentials, or error messages.

## Evidence

- Live collector observation showed the current hierarchy: `openclaw.node.tool.invoke` → `openclaw.node.tool.execute` → `openclaw.node.tool.system_run.authorize` / `openclaw.node.tool.system_run.run`.
- Collector attributes distinguished an exec-policy denial from sandbox precondition denials and reported sandbox requested/applied/provider/technology values.
- Real gateway → Windows node → MXC E2E passed both command execution and tray-data containment proofs.
- Branch-wide Opus/Codex review found no accepted actionable issues.
